name: Mars Canyons
near: Kaji-Sai (urban-type settlement, Ton district) — the turn-off from the highway is about 2.5–3 km west of the village; the red hills themselves are 3 km from Kaji-Sai.
elev: About 1,700–1,800 m: the Issyk-Kul shore is 1,607 m, Kaji-Sai village 1,740 m; the “Mars” hills rise a few dozen metres above the road. There are no exact measurements of the canyon's elevation in the sources (calculated from the heights of nearby points).
short: Red clay-and-sandstone hills and gullies near Kaji-Sai on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul, nicknamed “Mars” for the colour of the rock.
desc: The Mars Canyons are a ridge of red eroded hills between the south-shore highway and the Terskey Ala-Too, 3 km from the village of Kaji-Sai. It is not a true rock canyon but dozens of rain-carved channels and ridges of red clay and sandstone; from the upper points there is a panorama of Issyk-Kul and snowy peaks. The place is almost undeveloped: no ticket offices, signs or trails, and noticeably fewer people than at Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon 20 km to the west. The rock crumbles, and after rain the clay becomes slippery.
guide: Turn off the highway about 2.8 km west of the Kaji-Sai river — the landmark is an “unfinished multi-storey building” on the right — and drive along the dirt road/dry riverbed to the spot where the channel narrows; continue on foot. Climb any ridge: from here you see the red “Martian” folds, the turquoise Issyk-Kul and the snowy Terskey all at once — this is the main shot of the place. Come for sunset (17–19 h): the red colour of the rock intensifies noticeably, while by day it fades and it is hot. In spring, spiny anabasis bushes with red-yellow flowers bloom among the clay. Don't look for trails — there aren't any: walk along the ridges rather than the narrow gullies, and remember that the clay turns into a skating rink after rain.
see: Red eroded ridges and gullies; a panorama of Issyk-Kul and the Terskey Ala-Too from the upper points; sunset light; desert flora (anabasis). A good spot for drone photography (locationscout.net lists the place as a drone spot — you need a flying licence).
skip: You've already been to Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon and want something fundamentally different — the same red clays are here, just without infrastructure and crowds. You're going in the rain — the clay is slippery, and the dry channels may fill with water. You have a low-clearance car and don't want to walk 2–3 km from the highway.
diff: Easy: a 1–2 h walk over hills without trails, with little elevation gain; you only need sturdy shoes. Be careful on the crumbling clay ridges.
when: June–September (sunny, little rain, around +25 °C). Spring and autumn are also fine, but after rain the clay is impassable. In winter access is limited by the condition of the dirt road.
hours: Open area, open 24 hours (Google Maps, viewed 03.10.2026: “Daily: 24 hours a day”). There are no ticket offices, barriers or guards.
daytime: The “golden hour” before sunset (17:00–19:00) — the red colour of the rock intensifies; also sunrise. Avoid midday: harsh light and heat.
how: The Balykchy — Karakol highway along the southern shore. From Bishkek ~270–290 km, 4–4.5 h via the Boom Gorge and Balykchy; from Karakol ~120 km (about 2 h). The turn-off from the highway is 2.5–3 km west of Kaji-Sai (there is a sign; according to a 2022 description, the landmark is an unfinished building on the right), then 1–3 km along a dirt road and a dry riverbed to the red hills; people leave their car where the channel narrows and continue on foot. On foot from the highway it is about 3 km.
needcar: Yes: from the highway to the hills it is 1–3 km of dirt road. You can get there by taxi/with a tour or walk from the marshrutka (minibus) stop in Kaji-Sai (~3 km).
self: Yes, completely: there is no ticket office, guide or permits; you need offline maps (Maps.me/2GIS/Organic), water and shoes. The only difficulty is finding the turn-off, which has no sign, and not getting lost among identical gullies.
roadtype: Paved road along the Balykchy — Karakol highway; from the turn-off a dirt road and dry riverbed (gravel, sand, clay). In dry weather a passenger car can make it with care (locationscout.net: “4x4 not needed”; nomadcar.kg recommends high ground clearance); after rain the clay is slippery and impassable.
traveltime: From Bishkek 4–4.5 h (270–290 km); from Karakol ~2 h; from Barskoon ~1 h; from Tosor ~45 min; from Bokonbaevo/Ton ~20 min. Sightseeing — 1–2 h.
stay: In Kaji-Sai: Salima Resort, Legenda Health Resort, Solema guest house, private guesthouses (prices are not given in the sources). Yurt camps on the shore: Bel-Tam Yurt Camp (Bokonbaevo, ~20 min), Yurt Camp Sonun, Yurt Camp Kyzyl Bulak (at the turn-off to the canyon, a Google Maps point). 2025–2026 prices are not confirmed — check when booking.
net: Mobile coverage and internet disappear in the canyons themselves (nomadcar.kg; a 2024 blog: “limited reception”). In Kaji-Sai and on the highway there is Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage. Download offline maps in advance.
entry: Free: there is no official entrance or ticket office (2024 blog: “no official entrance point… free to visit”). In 2022 iXBT mentioned rumours of a summer fee for driving in — not confirmed by any 2024–2026 source. For comparison: at neighbouring Skazka the eco fee is 50–100 som/person.
transfer: Taxi from Ton/Bokonbaevo round trip with waiting — 1,200 som (July 2024). Jeep tour from Cholpon-Ata through the south-shore canyons — €470 per group of up to 6 people (Tripster, 2025–2026). Bishkek — Kaji-Sai marshrutka: the 2025 price is not confirmed.
bring: Water (1.5 L/person — no shade), a hat and sun protection, shoes with a tread (clay and scree), offline maps, cash (there are few ATMs in Kaji-Sai), a camera/drone (licensed), a windbreaker for the evening.
warn: No trails or signs — it is easy to get lost among identical gullies, so return before dark. The clay is slippery after rain; dry channels can quickly fill with water in a downpour — don't drive or walk along the channel in the rain. The ridges crumble — don't go near the edges. Don't leave belongings visible in the car.
food: In Kaji-Sai and on the highway — cafés with lagman, manty and shashlik; on the southern shore the classic option is smoked and dried Issyk-Kul fish by the road and in Bokonbaevo. There are no eateries at the canyon itself — bring food with you.
reviews: Google Maps (“Canyon ‘Mars’”): 4.8/5, 29 ratings as of 03.10.2026. Blogs (2022–2024): pros — deserted, free, a spectacular sunset, a panorama of the lake; cons — no signs, hard to find the turn-off, dusty dirt road, impassable after rain. No separate TripAdvisor listing was found.
p.sum: The Mars Canyons are a free “wild” stop on the southern shore between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Sai: turn off the Balykchy — Karakol highway 2.5–3 km west of Kaji-Sai (a sign; the landmark is an unfinished building), then 1–3 km of dirt road to the spot where you leave the car. It is most convenient by your own car or by taxi from a yurt camp in Ton/Bokonbaevo (about 1,200 som round trip with waiting, 2024); without a car — any south-shore marshrutka to Kaji-Sai and 3 km on foot. Combine with Manjyly-Ata (0.5 km) and Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon (20 km), come for sunset, and spend the night in a yurt camp on the shore.

p.iti.1.title: The south shore in 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek → Boom Gorge → Bokonbaevo (eagle-hunter show) → Manjyly-Ata → Mars at sunset → night at Bel-Tam/Kaji-Sai. Day 2: sunrise at Skazka (Fairy Tale) (20 km) → Barskoon or Jeti-Oguz → Karakol.
p.iti.2.title: Logical combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Along the highway from west to east: Tuz-Kol → Bokonbaevo → Manjyly-Ata → Mars → Shatyly Panorama → Skazka (Fairy Tale) → Tosor/Tamga → Barskoon → Juuku → Jeti-Oguz → Karakol.
p.season: April–May: green slopes, anabasis in bloom, rain is possible — the clay is slippery. June–August: dry, +25…+30 °C by day, go at sunrise/sunset; beach season in Kaji-Sai. September–October: the best time — dry, soft light. November–March: cold and windy, driving on the dirt road depends on snow/mud.
p.budget.economy: ≈1,500–2,500 som/person per day: Bishkek — Kaji-Sai marshrutka 500–600, free entry, private sector 500–1,000, food 500–800.
p.budget.comfort: ≈5,000–9,000 som/person: a taxi/car from Bishkek or a jeep tour (Tripster €470 per group of up to 6), yurt camp $17–54, a guest house with meals.
p.permits: Not needed. Entry is free, no ticket offices.
p.access: With kids — yes, for a short walk along the ridges (scree — hold their hand). For older people — only near the parking spot. With a wheelchair — no (sand, clay). With a dog — possible, but it is hot and there is no water.
